warning: Prototype passage candidates only. No full scripture text, final commentary, therapy, ritual instruction, or spiritual authority.

passages.title: Steadiness in Action
passages.plain_meaning: The passage is commonly read as an invitation to act with steadiness rather than becoming owned by success or failure.
passages.beginner_note: Start with the action in front of you. Let the result matter, but do not let it become your whole identity.
passages.context_boundary: This is a reflection candidate, not therapy, medical advice, ritual instruction, or a promise of instant peace.
passages.reflection_question: What is one duty I can do clearly today without turning the outcome into my identity?
passages.carry_action: Choose one small task and do it slowly, cleanly, and without checking for praise.
passages.reviewer_note: Needs translation edition, commentary lane, and source rights review before public answer use.
passages.no_go: Do not use this passage to shame people for grief, illness, exhaustion, or real-world constraints.

passages.title: The Good and the Merely Pleasant
passages.plain_meaning: The passage is often read as a distinction between what is deeply good and what is only immediately pleasing.
passages.beginner_note: A calm path is not always the easy path. The first step is to name which choice gives depth, not just relief.
passages.context_boundary: This is a source-guided reflection, not moral policing, family advice, or spiritual authority.
passages.reflection_question: Which option before me feels pleasant now, and which option still feels clean tomorrow?
passages.carry_action: Delay one impulsive choice long enough to name the good you are protecting.
passages.reviewer_note: Needs Upanishad-specific commentary context and careful wording for modern ethical questions.
passages.no_go: Do not turn this into judgment of another person's life, relationship, health, or emergency decision.

passages.title: Two Kinds of Knowing
passages.plain_meaning: The passage is often associated with a distinction between lower and higher forms of knowledge.
passages.beginner_note: Some learning gathers facts. Some learning changes how you stand in the world. VedaPath should help users see the difference.
passages.context_boundary: This is an educational layer, not a ranking of people, schools, faiths, or modern disciplines.
passages.reflection_question: What am I trying to collect, and what am I trying to understand?
passages.carry_action: Turn one broad question into a narrower source question before seeking an answer.
passages.reviewer_note: Needs Sanskrit terms, commentary variants, and category caution before deeper public use.
passages.no_go: Do not use this passage to dismiss science, scholarship, work skills, or practical knowledge.

passages.title: Held With Restraint
passages.plain_meaning: The passage is often approached as a meditation on living in the world without grasping at it as possession.
passages.beginner_note: The calm move is not escape. It is a different relationship with what you use, hold, and release.
passages.context_boundary: This is reflection support, not economic, legal, property, or renunciation advice.
passages.reflection_question: What am I holding so tightly that it has stopped serving the work?
passages.carry_action: Use one thing with care today, then leave it without needing it to define you.
passages.reviewer_note: Needs translation-rights review and school-specific interpretation boundaries.
passages.no_go: Do not use this passage to pressure someone to give up safety, money, shelter, or responsibility.

passages.title: Conduct After Learning
passages.plain_meaning: This passage is often used to frame conduct, respect, truthfulness, and responsibility after learning.
passages.beginner_note: Learning becomes visible through conduct. The next step is not more noise, but cleaner action.
passages.context_boundary: This is educational reflection, not legal advice, institutional policy, or social command.
passages.reflection_question: Where should my learning become visible in behavior today?
passages.carry_action: Choose one honest, respectful action that makes learning practical.
passages.reviewer_note: Needs careful handling because conduct instructions can be overextended into modern authority claims.
passages.no_go: Do not use this passage to override consent, law, safety, or personal boundaries.

passages.title: Reflect and Choose
passages.plain_meaning: The passage is often read as honoring reflection and personal agency after instruction is given.
passages.beginner_note: A source can guide without replacing the person who must choose. That is the product posture too.
passages.context_boundary: This is a reflection candidate, not a command, oracle, or final authority over personal life.
passages.reflection_question: What have I heard clearly, and what choice is actually mine to make?
passages.carry_action: Write the next choice in one plain sentence, then take responsibility for one small step.
passages.reviewer_note: Needs commentary context because the speaker, setting, and theological frame matter.
passages.no_go: Do not use this passage to pretend every decision is easy, isolated, or free of real constraints.
